title: Overcoming a Habit of Comparison
paragraphs: For years, Damar found himself constantly comparing his career progress to former classmates, tracking their promotions and purchases through social media in a way that left him feeling perpetually inadequate regardless of his own genuine achievements.

This habit intensified during a particularly difficult year when a close friend's business succeeded rapidly while Damar's own more modest venture struggled simply to remain profitable month after month.

A conversation with his father, who admitted having struggled with similar comparisons decades earlier, helped Damar recognize that measuring his life against curated glimpses of others' success was fundamentally an unfair and distorted comparison.

Rather than eliminating social media entirely, Damar experimented with deliberately limiting his usage and redirecting that attention toward tracking his own progress against his personal goals from previous years instead.

The shift felt awkward initially, since old habits of comparison resurfaced frequently during moments of insecurity, requiring consistent, deliberate redirection rather than a single decisive change of mindset.

Two years into this practice, Damar reports feeling considerably more contentment with his own path, noting that the comparison habit had cost him years of genuine gratitude for progress he had already made.
